comparisons.identifies: model capability at fixed input (4B-I vs 32B-I)
comparisons.cannot: say anything about the device tier: both arms ran on the H100, and H1 is 4B on cloud hardware, not a device measurement
comparisons.evidence: StudyClean input_identity: prompt tokens 845/845 exact, H1 replays K3's own requests; same vLLM 0.31.0 FA3, both greedy 512

comparisons.identifies: model capability at fixed input on the RICH construction
comparisons.cannot: separate capability from host: K1 ran on GPU 3 and H2 on GPU 1. The SAN cell (30/30 letters) is the evidence that the card does not move greedy letters, so this is a near-identical, not an identical, host
comparisons.evidence: prompt tokens 845/845 exact; same stack and decoding

comparisons.identifies: the value of history at a fixed model, stride, frame size and format: H3 is exactly D2's frames filtered to t >= qt-120, so D2 strictly contains H3's frames
comparisons.cannot: separate history from the header (H3 keeps D2's 'from the session start' header, which is false for H3 when qt > 120); and it cannot be read as a clean cold-latency contrast, because RH4's server ran with prefix_caching=True while StudyClean's ran with it OFF
comparisons.evidence: tokens INSIDE 5,622 vs 12,710; OLDER 5,603 vs 14,857; qt<=120 3,505 = 3,505 (identical input, built-in null)

comparisons.identifies: nothing on its own as a single factor: RICH vs RECENT moves the window, the frame count and the resolution together under one token budget
comparisons.cannot: attribute the sign flip to history length alone; the audit already records that window, frame count and resolution move together
comparisons.evidence: same model, stack, host, greedy t=0.0; audit comparability table

comparisons.identifies: the same RICH-vs-RECENT reallocation as K1-K3, but read by 4B-I
comparisons.cannot: be used as a capability claim; both arms are the same model
